stops.note: 'bed, couch'; klinikós meant a physician who visits patients in bed
a bedside physician; also, in the early Church, a person baptised on their sickbed
bedside teaching, pioneered by Herman Boerhaave at Leiden in the early 1700s, spread to Edinburgh and London; 'clinical' for coolly detached dates from the 1900s

current_meaning: relating to the treatment of patients; coldly efficient
